name: Dawn hope
desc: The night is survived. First light, and the damage still showing.

sets.place: hilltop at dawn, sunrise on the horizon, empty road below, long shadows

shots.desc: sunrise over a wide empty valley, first light on the horizon, long shadows, cloudless sky, no humans
face turned up into the first sunlight, steady gaze, closed mouth, warm rim light on the cheek, close-up
figure standing alone at the crest of a hill, backlit by the rising sun, long shadow stretching toward camera, wide shot
sunlight breaking across dew-covered grass, water droplets catching the light, close-up, no humans

why: Hope only reads if the cost is still visible, so this template sets wear 3 - torn, stained, exhausted - and then lights it golden. The contradiction between a wrecked costume and warm light is the whole emotional trick, and it works because both halves are concrete: the damage is garment tags, the warmth is an ffmpeg grade. emotion:resolve gives a steady gaze and a closed mouth rather than a grin, which is what keeps it from tipping over into victory. tilt_u on the establish is the house move for power, scale and awe. Use it as an ending, or as the turn at the bottom of a second act.
note: transition 'fade_white' is advisory - short.py renders hard cuts. Two real caveats. First, cue 'triumphant_build' is generated by ACE-Step 1.5, which has no hit-point conditioning and cannot spot to picture, so the swell will NOT land on the sunrise - it arrives wherever it arrives. Second, wear is resolved as max() across movie, chapter and scene in compile.py and never decreases, so setting 3 here locks every later scene in the film to 3 or higher. Drop it to 0 if this template opens your film rather than closing it.
